title: Great App but Expensive
body:
I have used this app premium version for two months now. It has been amazing. It is exactly what I need. A habit tracker where I can actually analyze the data to see which habits I still need to work on. 

I gave it 4 stars because I’ve been having issues with its timer feature. If I turn on the timer and move to another app, the timer stops working. If I play music or a video, the timer stops working. It’s very frustrating especially since I like using its Pomodoro feature to complete tasks. It throws my data off. 

Another feature that needs to be fixed is displaying data if you completed some of the work. There are some goals that are time based. For example, if the goal is 30 minutes a day, but you only completed 20 minutes. It would be nice to see it in the stats section. You only see if it is completed or not on the calendar even though you have a symbol for some done. 

Additionally, I wish I could export my data to an excel file. If I’m tracking my goals this would take it to the next level.

I know that many have complained about the price increase. I am paying about $35 a year for it. This is pricey but I think it’s worth it. Now if it jumps up to $80 that would be really steep.

Many others give you your stats since the birth of the app which means if you fall off for 4 months you can never get to the rewarding acknowledgment of high percentages.

title: A gem
body: Honestly, this app is just perfect. It does one thing extremely well. I'm always amazed when people complain about an app being too simple. It's just an elegant design and it achieves everything it needs to achieve. And 11 bucks a year or whatever it is seems reasonable for that. It’s a really helpful app. That said, there are a couple ways in which I think the app could be improved. I have one broad feature in mind and one specific feature in mind. Firstly, it would be nice to have some more statistics or visualizations or insight into how you're doing versus the past. Are your relapses getting further and further apart, or are they coming closer together? Just some insight into how this compares to your best ever trend. Maybe resets per month, stuff like that. The second thing is much more simple and concrete. Basically, it would be nice to be able to edit the units without just selecting one. There's an app called Countdown that does this really nicely. You can select each unit independently of the others. So it has every unit from years, quarters, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, and seconds. You know, I might have that slightly wrong, but it's roughly along those lines. And for each unit, you can tick whether to include it or not. In practice, I don't think that people often want to skip a bunch of units. Like, nobody's going to do years and seconds. But it's actually really nice for the widgets. In the app, I think you guys do a great job. For the widget, it would be nice for people who are trying to quit something right at the beginning and they're proud of just getting 5, 10, 15 minutes. But let's say you're trying to not interrupt someone and you're in a meeting. I mean, you might be proud of 20 minutes, but the lowest unit you have is hours. So I think it would just give you guys more flexibility if you keep the app exactly the same. But for the widgets, let people choose how to format the duration string and specifically what units to include. Anyway, thank you for building such a fantastic product. And I really appreciate the time and effort and attention to detail that you put into this product.

title: AMAZING for the ADHD brain!
body:
For a person with ADHD, basically every other productivity / habit tracking app out there overcomplicates the work of setting up your habits AND tracking them. 

I want good habits, I don’t need a million bells and whistles and charts. In fact, for most of us with ADHD those are the fastest ways to get hyper focused, distracted, and then bored / quit. 

This app is BEAUTIFUL and simple to use - from the lovely little icon on my Home Screen to the pretty and clean organization of my daily apps. It lets me add a motivation (the “value” behind the goal - which has been shown repeatedly to make the goal more likely to be completed when seen), it clears the items off of my screen when I’ve completed them for the day (that’s one of the view options), it allows me to log a note or entry with my count that is easy to retrieve and see all notes at a glance, and the best part, it allows me to set a reminder for a specific time that only goes off when the goal is unmet!

This app is a lifesaver! My only suggestion, start small - pick 2-3 easily achievable daily goals (rather than weekly): floss your teeth, make your bed in the am, take your vitamins/meds, etc). Once you start feeling proud for checking things off, add no more than 1-2 new goals a week or 1 new weekly goal! GOOD LUCK with your new habits! I’m rooting for you!

title: Small suggestion that would drastically help
body:
I love this app so much. It has helped motivate me with so many daily and weekly goals. 

There is one update I hope the developers will one day work on. There is no way to easily track/view your stats on a WEEKLY goal basis. For instance: one of my weekly goals is to do 100 push-ups. When viewing the graph of this bar you can view by WEEK MONTH or YEAR. When viewing the WEEK stat it shows a breakdown of individual days rather than a single number. This should be a separate section labeled DAYS. The WEEK layout should simply show the TOTAL FOR THE WEEK rather than showing how much each day. For example, when I’m trying to see how Many push-ups I did this week vs last week it should just show one single number of the TOTAL of last week and the total of this week. Instead it shows a daily breakdown. 

That would be the one thing that would help users really track their weekly progress with ONE TOTAL number being shown rather than the entire weeks worth of individual daily stats.

title: Good base but missing potential
body: The NFC capability is great as well as many customizable features like weekly habits.  However, the progress reporting is lacking which takes away from clarity of improvement and motivation to continue.  For example, in the previous week’s report, there is no reference to total successes, fails and skips.  You have to add them up yourself.  It gives you a total successes percentage but not the raw numbers that percentage is calculated with.  I am available if a developer would like to know more.  I have experience with other habit tracking apps that have features I think are worth contemplating.

title: App keeps getting better
body:
This is by far the best habit tracker in App Store. I have, however, two improvement requests:

1- Add setting to always show best streak. Right now the only way to see the best streak is by having at least three check-ins in a row. Not having that visible at all times is demotivating if you broke the chain and you are trying to recover.

2- Drag and drop from main view. The only way to reorder now is by going to the settings. This is not the best scenario since I am reordering the habits by the effectivity all the time to focus on the ones that need improvement.

PLEASE add those improvements and I will update the review to 5 stars.

title: Good app but please add "yellow"
body: I have come across lots of physical health apps, but this is my first for habits and better living.  I really like the simplicity, ease of taking notes, and graphs.  I don't like the red and green with no in between.  It's like I either pass or fail.  They need the "yellow light" for, "proceed slowly with caution."  Meaning you didn't fail but you didn't meet your goal either, as was my very first experience using the app.  If they had a "yellow" then the journal part would be real handy to take note of what was working and what went wrong.  The skip function is great for when you actually aren't focused on that habit or goal that day.

It'd be perfect if you could add a feature to label a habit as positive or negative 🙏
